sf69e59a477.details: From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen. Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song. Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame. Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale. Screening times vary by day.

s1851df7c7d.details: “There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.” This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession. In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop. Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us. se1a6c7e1c6.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

s86febcf073.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. Located in Toronto, the Bata Shoe Museum (BSM) regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artefacts, chosen from a collection of almost 14,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions. Over the course of this year we will continuing to present The Great Divide: Footwear in the Age of Enlightenment and our newest exhibit, All Dolled Up: Fashioning Cultural Expectations explores how dolls and the clothes they wear have historically promoted complex cultural ideas about gender, body image, social status and fashion consumption in the West and how these ideas are being challenged today.

A love letter to our enemies. A transfeminist fantasia. A bad idea and a good time. Come into the mansion. Nothing bad could possibly happen. Join Shel Silverstein, Gloria Steinum, Hugh Hefner, and various prey animals in the labyrinthine Playboy mansion to explore party planning, 70’s idealism, and the neo-liberal melodrama of the trans scapegoat via popular children’s music. In We Quit Theatre ’s signature mix of delight and iconoclasm, GLORY! mines the political, aesthetic, and libidinal contradictions of the ‘70s to grapple with our present moment of crisis. A foil to second-wave feminism and a deep throated scream for trans aliveness, GLORY! is a party you don’t want to miss. Sexsmith credits Leonard Cohen’s influence as the inspiration for writing his first proper song, “Speaking With The Angel”. As with previous “Sexsmith Sings...” concerts, Ron will perform two solo sets comprised of his favourite Cohen compositions – except for “Hallelujah” which has been done to death. The show will include anecdotes and personal insights into Leonard's songs in what will truly be a full circle moment and an intimate and loving tribute.
